posting_excerpt:
of AI to clearly mapping how AI will impact different functions, from fund formation and side letter negotiation to regulatory compliance and investor reporting.

 - Understanding and navigating the requirements of regulated financial institutions, including confidentiality expectations, information barriers, vendor due diligence, and the scrutiny that comes with SEC oversight.

 - Partnering with deal teams at sponsors, sovereign investors, and law firms on transaction workflows - building diligence grids, closing checklists, and document review processes that run at deal speed across M&A, growth, and venture transactions.


WHAT YOU BRING

You come from the world of funds, asset management, or M&A; but you've never been content with how things have always been done. You may have practiced as a private funds associate at a leading law firm, negotiating fund documents, side letters, and co-investment structures. Perhaps you've worked in-house at an asset manager, running lean legal processes across the full fund lifecycle. Maybe you've built your career in compliance, managing regulatory obligations, exams, and investor requirements at an investment firm. Or you may have cut your teeth in M&A or ECVC, running diligence and negotiating transaction documents under deal pressure. Either way, you know how asset management and funds teams — in-house and at law firms — think, work, and (sometimes) struggle and you're ready to help them level up with technology.

You'll thrive in this role if you:

 - Hold a law degree (JD or equivalent) and bring 3+ years of experience in a private funds or M&A/ECVC practice at a law firm, in-house at an asset management firm, or in a regulatory or compliance function - ideally with exposure to multiple fund strategies, structures, deal types, or jurisdictions.

 - Understand the asset management context: fund lifecycles, GP/LP dynamics, side letter and MFN obligations, subscription documents, DDQs, and the regulatory landscape - from the Advisers Act and Marketing Rule to Form ADV, Form PF, and SEC exam readiness.

 - Are tech-curious and product-savvy. Not necessarily a coder, but passionate about navigating technical conversations, especially around things like generative AI, technology implementation, innovation and productivity.

 - Communicate clearly and confidently with diverse stakeholders, from general counsel to chief compliance officers, and from investor relations teams to engineers. I.e. translating across disciplines is second nature to you.

 - Bring structure to ambiguity and energy to complexity; and enjoy being the calm, credible presence in a fast-moving environment.

 - Understand how to evaluate and improve existing processes as a direct result of new and emerging technologies - whether that's streamlining fund formation and side letter review, tracking investor obligations across funds, accelerating DDQ and RFP responses, or strengthening compliance and marketing reviews.

 - Are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable juggling multiple client relationships at once.

 - Care deeply about quality, but don't get stuck in perfectionism - you get things done, and you make them better over time.

 - Understand the commercial realities of asset management: fundraising timelines, investor expectations, regulatory scrutiny, pressure on legal and compliance budgets, and the balance between speed and rigor when capital is on the line.
